title: Universal Bound and Phase Transition in Many-Body Fermionic Non-Gaussianity
authors: Masahiro Hoshino, Ryota Matsuda, Yuto Ashida
abstract: Fermionic non-Gaussianity is a resource for universal quantum computation that can be generated by interactions in quantum many-body systems. Using the magic Rényi entropy (MRE) as a measure of non-Gaussianity, we derive its universal upper bound and Haar mean, proving that typical Haar-random states attain the maximal MRE density of $\ln(4/3)$ per Majorana in the large-system limit. We also show that the MRE can differ extensively between states with identical covariance matrices. To investigate how non-Gaussianity grows toward this maximal density, we evolve a Gaussian state in imaginary and real time under the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Hamiltonian. By varying the imaginary- and real-time durations, we identify a first-order transition marked by a kink in the MRE density and spontaneous breaking of the permutation symmetry among the four copies used to evaluate the MRE. This transition represents a qualitative change in the non-Gaussianity of the state that is not reflected in the thermal free energy.
summary: This work analyzes fermionic non-Gaussianity using the magic Rényi entropy (MRE) to characterize quantum states in many-body systems. The authors establish a universal upper bound for MRE and demonstrate that the MRE can detect a first-order phase transition in the SYK model that is not visible in the system's thermal free energy. This highlights MRE as a sensitive probe of quantum correlations beyond standard thermodynamic measures.
main_problem: The paper investigates fermionic non-Gaussianity, a resource for quantum computation, by deriving its universal upper bound and analyzing its growth dynamics.
main_result: They prove that typical Haar-random states achieve a maximal MRE density of ln(4/3) per Majorana, and they identify a first-order phase transition in the MRE density for the SYK model that is invisible to the thermal free energy.
method: The analysis uses the magic Rényi entropy (MRE) as a diagnostic tool, employing path integrals, saddle-point approximations, and solving Schwinger-Dyson equations.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum many-body systems, specifically utilizing the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) Hamiltonian to model interacting dynamics, and analyzing purity measures for fermionic states.

important_parameters: Large-system limit (N->infinity), imaginary and real-time durations ($ eta, t$), and the coupling strength J in the SYK model.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on the saddle-point approximation to determine the leading exponential behavior in the large-N limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram and the MRE density of the KM state, showing a kink marking a first-order transition.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the universal upper bound for MRE in random states, to analyzing the dynamics of the MRE in the SYK model, and finally deriving the necessary saddle-point equations to confirm the phase transition structure.
why_interesting: The detection of a non-Gaussianity transition that decouples from the standard thermal free energy is a powerful diagnostic tool for characterizing quantum phases in strongly interacting systems.
